author: Chris Schommer
title: Cole Carrigg keeps raking in loss to Dodgers
desc: Cole Carrigg went 3-for-5 in a loss to the Dodgers with two doubles, three runs scored, and two RBI.
impact: Carrigg continues a productive stretch at the plate, driving in two or more runs in four of his last five contests. The outfielder has rewarded manager Warren Schaeffer with one of the more dynamic options in the Rockies lineup, carrying a .978 OPS with four home runs, 21 RBI, 21 runs scored, and two stolen bases through 25 games.

author: Chris Schommer
title: Ezequiel Tovar goes deep in loss to Dodgers
desc: Ezequiel Tovar went 1-for-3 in a loss to the Dodgers with a home run, two runs scored, two RBI, and one walk.
impact: Tovar has provided mixed results at the plate, collecting hits in six of his last 13 contests. The infielder remains one of the more underwhelming bats in the Rockies lineup to this point, batting .209 with eight home runs, 32 RBI, 31 runs scored, and five stolen bases across 86 games.

author: Chris Schommer
title: Tyler Freeman chips in two hits, steal in loss to Dodgers
desc: Tyler Freeman went 2-for-3 in a loss to the Dodgers with one walk and one stolen base.
impact: Freeman continues a steady stretch at the plate, picking up hits in 11 of his last 18 contests. The outfielder offers manager Warren Schaeffer another stable option in a streaky Rockies lineup, batting .274 with three home runs, 23 RBI, six steals, and 26 runs scored through 61 games.

author: Chris Schommer
title: Kyle Freeland rocked early in no-decision
desc: Kyle Freeland allowed six earned runs on nine hits while striking out two over five innings in Monday's loss to the Dodgers.
impact: Freeland continues an underwhelming stretch on the mound, allowing three earned runs or more in 11 of his last 13 trips to the mound. The left-hander remains one of many dismal starting options in the Rockies rotation for manager Warren Schaeffer, posting a 7.46 ERA and 1.61 WHIP with a 2-7 record and 7.7 K/9 ratio across 16 starts.

author: Chris Schommer
title: Heliot Ramos drives in five in rout of Blue Jays
desc: Heliot Ramos went 3-for-5 in a 10-1 win over the Blue Jays with two home runs, one triple, three runs scored, and five RBI.
impact: Ramos continues a dynamic stretch at the plate of late, recording hits in 13 of his last 16 contests. The outfielder has rewarded manager Tony Vitello as one of the more impactful bats in an inconsistent Giants lineup, carrying an .806 OPS with eight home runs, 28 RBI, and 27 runs scored across 52 games.

author: Chris Schommer
title: Luis Arraez swipes base in rout of Blue Jays
desc: Luis Arraez went 1-for-4 in a win over the Blue Jays with one stolen base.
impact: Arraez continues an impactful stretch at the plate, collecting hits in 11 of his last 13 contests. The infielder remains one of the few consistent options in the Giants lineup for manager Tony Vitello, slashing .325 with four home runs, seven steals, 33 RBI, and 45 runs scored across 85 games.

author: Ari Koslow
title: Ranger Suarez (adductor) hopeful to avoid IL stint
desc: The Red Sox remain hopeful Ranger Suarez can avoid an IL stint.
impact: Boston is expected to see how Suarez feels on Tuesday. There should be an update on him later in the week.

author: Brenton Kemp
title: Brandon Lockridge (knee) transferred to 60-day IL
desc: The Brewers have transferred outfielder Brandon Lockridge (knee) to the 60-day injured list.
impact: The Brewers needed to clear a 40-man roster spot for utility man Greg Jones coming up from Triple-A Nashville, with David Hamilton (hamstring) headed to the 10-day IL. Lockridge has been out since May 9 and is expected to return in late July.

author: Chris Schommer
title: Victor Bericoto drives in two as Giants rout Blue Jays
desc: Victor Bericoto went 2-for-4 in Monday's 10-1 win over the Blue Jays with two runs scored, two RBI, and one stolen base.
impact: Bericoto has heated up at the plate, registering hits in eight of his last nine contests. The outfielder has offered manager Tony Vitello another impactful bat in the Giants lineup since being called up, batting .314 with four home runs, eight RBI, seven runs scored, and one stolen base across 22 games.

author: Brenton Kemp
title: Greg Jones selected from Triple-A
desc: Brewers utility man Greg Jones has been selected from Triple-A Nashville.
impact: The Brewers needed an infielder from Nashville to replace David Hamilton (hamstring), who was placed on the injured list on Monday. Jones has appeared in just 11 games with the Brewers this season, but has hit .289 with one homer and 21 stolen bases in 40 games with Nashville, bringing a speed element to the table in Hamilton's absence.

author: Brenton Kemp
title: David Hamilton (hamstring) placed on 10-day IL
desc: The Brewers have placed infielder David Hamilton on the 10-day injured list with a left hamstring strain.
impact: Hamilton was injured during Monday's 4-3 win over the Cardinals and will need some time on the injured list to heal. The 28-year-old has hit .240 with three homers, 18 stolen bases, and a .650 OPS through 74 games this season.

author: Chris Schommer
title: Landen Roupp cruises through eight in rout of Blue Jays
desc: Landen Roupp allowed one earned run on three hits and two walks while striking out five over eight innings in Monday's win over the Blue Jays.
impact: Roupp has provided mixed results on the mound of late, allowing four earned runs or more in four of his last eight trips to the mound. The right-hander remains one of the more inconsistent arms in the Giants rotation for manager Tony Vitello, posting a 4.27 ERA and 1.31 WHIP with a 6-8 record and 9.6 K/9 ratio across 18 starts.

author: Chris Schommer
title: Jose Altuve goes deep in loss to Nationals
desc: Jose Altuve went 1-for-5 in a loss to the Nationals with a three-run home run.
impact: Altuve continues a steady stretch at the plate, registering hits in six of his last nine contests. The veteran remains one of many streaky bats in the Astros lineup for manager Joe Espada, batting .235 with nine home runs, 25 RBI, 42 runs scored, and two stolen bases across 69 games.

author: Chris Schommer
title: Yainer Diaz goes yard in loss to Nationals
desc: Yainer Diaz went 2-for-4 in loss to the Nationals with a home run, two runs scored, and two RBI.
impact: Diaz continues a solid stretch at the plate of late, collecting hits in seven of his last 10 contests. The catcher remains one of many streaky options in the Astros lineup for manager Joe Espada, batting .248 with five home runs, 21 RBI, and 15 runs scored across 40 games this season.

author: Ari Koslow
title: Dominic Canzone slated to step into full-time role
desc: Mariners GM Jerry Dipoto indicated Tuesday that Dominic Canzone will have a full-time spot in the lineup moving forward.
impact: Canzone has made his first four starts of the season against left-handed pitchers in the past month. He is slashing .273/.349/.551 on the season with 14 home runs so far.
